hook: Corinna Cortes earned a masters degree in physics from the University of Copenhagen before completing a PhD in computer science at the University of Rochester in 1993. She joined AT&T Bell Labs in 1989, where she spent more than a decade in the Adaptive Systems Research Group led by Larry Jackel. There she and Vladimir Vapnik developed the soft margin support vector machine, an extension that made support vector machines practical for real world classification problems with noisy, non separable data. Their 1995 paper on support vector networks became one of the most cited papers in machine learning. She later moved to Google, where she founded and now leads Google Research New York as a Vice President, overseeing large scale machine learning research across multiple international teams.

quick_facts: Born in Denmark in 1961 and earned a PhD in computer science from the University of Rochester in 1993
Spent more than a decade at AT&T Bell Labs in the Adaptive Systems Research Group
Co developed the soft margin support vector machine with Vladimir Vapnik, described in their 1995 paper Support Vector Networks
Received the AT&T Science and Technology Medal in 2000 for work on data mining in very large data sets
Shared the ACM Paris Kanellakis Theory and Practice Award with Vapnik in 2008
Vice President of Google Research, having founded and now leading its New York City lab
